title: Power Automate: schedule desktop flows directly with scheduled triggers
summary: Hold: Microsoft now documents scheduled triggers, including their prerequisites, schedule-management permissions, execution connections and enable/disable controls, which the briefing reports as unpublished. The roadmap facts and data-policy controls match their sources, but the default-state field and advice about monitoring direct scheduled runs need correction; Learn also describes the feature as preview despite the roadmap's Launched status.

claims.claim: Scheduled triggers let makers schedule desktop flows directly from the automation center without an intermediary scheduled cloud flow.
claims.quote: Scheduled triggers enable makers to run desktop flows on a recurring schedule directly from the Power Automate automation center, eliminating the need to create and manage intermediary scheduled cloud flows.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes daily, weekly, monthly, hourly and custom recurrence.
claims.quote: Users can configure daily, weekly, monthly, hourly, or custom recurrence patterns

claims.claim: Users can select the execution machine or machine group.
claims.quote: select the execution machine or machine group

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a central view of upcoming scheduled runs.
claims.quote: monitor upcoming scheduled runs from a centralized experience

claims.claim: The roadmap describes support for attended and unattended desktop flows.
claims.quote: a more intuitive scheduling experience for attended and unattended desktop flows.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"
claims.fix: Keep the roadmap status, but add: 'The roadmap lists Launched; Microsoft Learn describes Scheduled triggers as preview and says availability is being gradually rolled out across regions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe scheduled triggers or where makers create and manage them.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select **Automation center**.

claims.claim: Power Automate documents triggering desktop flows from cloud flows using events, schedules and buttons.
claims.quote: Power Automate enables you to trigger desktop flows from cloud flows using events, schedules, and buttons.

claims.claim: The cloud-flow route requires a registered machine or machine group.
claims.quote: A registered [machine](manage-machines) or [machine group](manage-machine-groups) that will run the triggered desktop flows.

claims.claim: The cloud-flow route requires a work or school account.
claims.quote: A work or school account.

claims.claim: The cloud-flow route requires a configured desktop flow connection.
claims.quote: A configured [desktop flow connection](desktop-flow-connections).

claims.claim: The automation center is a monitoring hub for automation activity.
claims.quote: the automation center serves as a centralized hub to monitor and manage automation activity within your environment.

claims.claim: The automation center has a Runs page for cloud and desktop flow execution data.
claims.quote: **Runs**: View and analyze cloud and desktop flow execution data with filtering options for overview, run history, and current desktop flow runs.

claims.claim: The automation center has a Machines page for machine and machine group status.
claims.quote: **Machines**: Manage and monitor machine and machine group status and connectivity.

claims.claim: The scheduled cloud flow's owner is part of how its run is governed.
claims.quote: If the flow is a **scheduled** or **automated** flow, after the owner changes, the flow runs under the license of the new owner and uses their Power Platform request limits.
claims.fix: Add 'Change the owner of a cloud flow' (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/change-cloud-flow-owner) to sources for the ownership premise. The updated page still supports this statement.

claims.claim: The desktop flow connection is part of how a cloud-triggered run is governed.
claims.quote: When you create a desktop flow connection, you allow Power Automate to create a Windows session on your machine to run your desktop flows.

claims.claim: Data policy checks govern cloud flows and the desktop flows they call.
claims.quote: Users can't run desktop flows from a cloud flow if the desktop flow violates any data loss prevention policy.

claims.claim: Learn does not fully explain which ownership, connection-licensing and connector-policy checks from the cloud-flow route apply to direct schedules.
claims.quote: Searched: scheduled triggers desktop flows data policies licence connection creator. Read schedule-desktop-flows, trigger-desktop-flows, prevent-data-loss, licensing/types and pay-as-you-go-meters; schedule prerequisites name run-mode entitlements but not the connection-creator licensing rule.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The arrival behaviour is not stated, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote:
To activate the trigger immediately after you create it, turn on **Enable**.
4. Select **Save**.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'user-opt-in'. Replace 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival' with 'Where available, makers create a schedule and turn on Enable to activate it; leaving Enable off saves it as disabled.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows and remove the question asking whether an administrator must enable the capability. Targeted searches found no feature-wide admin enable switch.

claims.claim: No source says existing flows or schedules are changed on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: scheduled triggers desktop flows admin enable Power Platform. Read roadmap record and schedule-desktop-flows; these describe creating new schedules, not automatic changes to existing flows or schedules.

claims.claim: A recurring schedule starts desktop flows automatically.
claims.quote: Scheduled triggers enable makers to run desktop flows on a recurring schedule

claims.claim: The roadmap does not identify the identity or connection used by scheduled runs.
claims.quote: Users can configure daily, weekly, monthly, hourly, or custom recurrence patterns, select the execution machine or machine group, and monitor upcoming scheduled runs from a centralized experience.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not describe additional data access beyond the desktop flow itself.
claims.quote: Scheduled Triggers simplify desktop automation management and provide a more intuitive scheduling experience for attended and unattended desktop flows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies classify desktop flow modules as Business, Non-business or Blocked.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as **Business**, **Non-business**, or **Blocked**.

claims.claim: Learn says noncompliant desktop flows are suspended.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: Whether scheduled runs undergo a different policy evaluation from cloud-triggered runs is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: scheduled triggers desktop DLP queue connection creator; scheduled triggers desktop flows data policies licence connection creator. Read schedule-desktop-flows and prevent-data-loss; neither describes a different DLP evaluation for direct schedules.

claims.quote: The user who needs to have the appropriate license is the creator of the connection.

claims.claim: Unattended mode runs without human supervision.
claims.quote: Unattended desktop flows are ideal for automating tasks that don't need human supervision.

claims.claim: Desktop flows time out if they do not run within 12 hours of being requested.
claims.quote: A time-out occurs when desktop flows don't run within 12 hours after being requested.

claims.claim: The queue page's orchestration rules apply to desktop flow runs scheduled by any user on the same device.
claims.quote: The presented orchestration rules apply to desktop flow runs scheduled by any user on the same device.

claims.where: controls[0].note; summary; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no setting or call for scheduled triggers specifically.
claims.quote:
Select **Disable** for an enabled trigger. Select **Enable** for a disabled trigger.

Disabling a scheduled trigger stops future scheduled runs without deleting its configuration.
claims.fix: Narrow controls[0].note, the summary and repeated absences to 'No tenant-wide or environment-wide availability switch for scheduled triggers is documented at the time of writing (November 2026).' Keep that tenant-scoped row's sides null. Replace the broad claim that no setting or call exists with 'Individual schedules can be disabled in Power Automate > Automation center > Manage > Scheduled triggers (Preview) > Overview > scheduled trigger > More commands > Disable.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows. Do not claim that schedules have no API: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/flowtrigger documents PATCH /flowtriggers(flowtriggerid), including statecode and statuscode.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide availability switch for scheduled triggers is documented on either UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: scheduled triggers Power Automate tenant disable; scheduled triggers desktop flows admin enable Power Platform; Flow trigger table entity reference. Read schedule-desktop-flows and flowtrigger reference; these give per-record controls, not a tenant availability switch.

claims.claim: Roles for scheduled triggers are not yet published.
claims.quote: users assigned the Power Automate *Operator* role can manage desktop-flow schedules, in addition to the schedule owner. They can create, view, update, enable or disable, and delete schedules.
claims.fix: Replace the roles absence with 'In environments where Scheduled triggers is available, the schedule owner and users assigned the Power Automate Operator role can manage schedules; Operator permissions apply across the assigned environment and do not themselves grant permission to edit desktop flow definitions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows.

claims.claim: Prerequisites for scheduled triggers are not yet published.
claims.quote:
A published desktop flow that you own or co-own.
- A machine or machine group registered in the same environment.
- A connection reference for the target machine or machine group.
claims.fix: Replace the prerequisites absence with 'Scheduled triggers require a work or school account with target-environment access, a published desktop flow you own or co-own, a machine or machine group registered in that environment, a connection reference for that target, and licensing and capacity for the selected attended or unattended mode.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics for scheduled triggers are not yet published.
claims.quote: This feature is being gradually rolled out across regions and might not be available yet in your region.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/schedule-desktop-flows; keep the roadmap's cloud list explicitly attributed to the record.

claims.quote: You can define a DLP policy that manages both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors. / The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether a direct schedule is evaluated through the desktop-flow connector.
claims.quote: Searched: scheduled triggers desktop flows data policies licence connection creator; scheduled triggers desktop DLP queue connection creator. Read schedule-desktop-flows and prevent-data-loss; they document execution connections and general connector governance, not this connector-evaluation mechanism.

claims.claim: Tenant-level data policies require the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: The automation center Runs and Machines pages can be relied on to review failed, queued or timed-out direct scheduled runs.

claims.fix: Replace the bullet with 'Confirm where direct scheduled executions appear before relying on automation center Runs and Machines for failure, queue and timeout monitoring.' The pages document general monitoring and projected Upcoming executions, not this specific monitoring coverage.
